parts.instruction: You will hear three different extracts. For questions 1-6, choose the answer (A, B or C) which fits best

questions.prompt: What do the people have different opinions about?

options.label: how interesting the programme is
the website design
the choice of the objects in the collection

questions.prompt: What does the woman like about the programme?

options.label: the consistency of quality in the interviews
the fact that it is educational
the way they talk about history

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the procedure in her department?

options.label: it could have been more efficient.
it does not necessarily help admit the best students.
going through the application forms is very tedious.

questions.prompt: What part of the man’s suggestion worries the woman?

options.label: if it would be any better than the current approach
if her colleagues would like it
if the procedure would be secure

questions.prompt: What is the project?

options.label: putting up decorations in a room
building an extension to a house
renovating a room

questions.prompt: Both speakers agree that

options.label: they could learn something from this work.
it is a relief that the work will start soon.
the process will cause certain discomfort.

parts.instruction: You will hear a young Arctic explorer called James Munro talking about his work. For questions 7-14, complete the sentences.

questions.prompt: James Munro and Greg Hamilton managed to finish an unsupported expedition through ________.
According to James, the only things helping them in this expedition were ________.
Both James’ parents worked as ________.
James believes that his love for ________ made him more interested in adventures.
The expedition to ________ in 1995 fascinated James.
James admires Nansen for his breadth as he was a diplomat, an explorer as well as a ________.
James is convinced that having control over one’s ________ is essential for an explorer.
James believes that making use of ________ is the best way for inexperienced explorers to get sponsors.

parts.instruction: You will hear an interview with a wildlife photographer. For questions 15-20, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best according to what you hear.

questions.prompt: The reason Adam tries to keep in touch with amateur colleagues is

options.label: he believes that they can teach him something.
he sees himself as amateur in some ways.
he finds pleasure in sharing his experience.
he was helped when he himself was a beginner.

questions.prompt: Adam sees professional ethics as

options.label: responsible use of technology.
respecting other photographers’ needs.
honesty about the way shots were made.
prioritising the needs of the subjects.

questions.prompt: What does Adam say about knowledge of wildlife?

options.label: it is has equal importance to technical competence.
There is an abundance of literature to give sufficient knowledge to aspiring photographers.
Knowing about wildlife results in taking better pictures.
Knowledge of technology is more important than that of wildlife.

questions.prompt: Mentioning recent shooting of bird species called ‘Great Crested Grebes’, Adam says that

options.label: he researched the way the bird behaves beforehand.
he chose his clothing carefully.
he tried his best to approach the bird’s nest as close as possible.
he made sure he didn’t disturb the birds.

questions.prompt: Adam concedes that he switched to digital from analog photography because

options.label: it was more advanced technically.
it was more financially viable.
it was easier to carry it around.
it was more simple to use.

questions.prompt: What is Adam’s attitude to getting the first prize in the competition?

options.label: he is grateful for the sizeable price
he is happy because the winning pictures hold special meaning to him
he feels lucky because he believes other people’s pictures were better
he feels pride for having his works chosen over other’s
